requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed as appworker UID/GID 1000 with /home/appworker, /bin/bash, a private group, and an owned mode-0700 home directory; it remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A root-owned PAM limits drop-in sets both soft and hard nofile limits to 8192 and nproc limits to 256. Fresh appworker login sessions directly reported those exact values and denied attempts to exceed them, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations show the same RHEL 10.0 release and 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 kernel. The implementation used the platform's existing user-management and PAM facilities, with no package installation or replacement, and package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral and final-state evidence. The appworker account exists, fresh login sessions receive and enforce the exact requested limits, and the original OS release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also completed coherently on node1.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The state-changing commands were directly connected to the requested outcome or mandatory restart protocol: account creation (cmd-38c351d70387414a), creation of the limits drop-in (cmd-dc585a96b8934f4d), and the required bounded node restart (cmd-3523d67fc0eb4d66). The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot ID, and recovered services, account/configuration, and login-limit behavior. Independent lifecycle observations corroborate the boot change, preserved platform, healthy package state, unchanged listener set apart from process IDs, and absence of failed services or executor-created temporary residue.
